articles.title: Global practice patterns of MR-linac use in head and neck radiotherapy: a survey by the international MR-Linac consortium
articles.summary: This international survey examines the clinical adoption of MR-Linac technology in head and neck cancer. It identifies that workflow inefficiencies and heterogeneous adaptive strategies remain key barriers, highlighting a need for AI-driven automation and standardized quality assurance to improve clinical integration.

articles.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: A Review in Neuroimaging
articles.summary: This review summarizes the role of artificial intelligence in neuro-oncological imaging, noting significant impacts on clinical and research workflows. AI-based image reconstruction, noise reduction, and automated segmentation are noted as key drivers for improving reproducibility and tumor quantification in clinical practice.

articles.title: Bioabsorbable spacer-assisted high-dose proton beam therapy for unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer of the body or tail: a feasibility and safety study
articles.summary: This study evaluates the technical feasibility and safety of using bioabsorbable spacers to enable high-dose proton beam therapy in patients with unresectable pancreatic cancer. Researchers note that while the approach is feasible, further research is required to fully characterize the risk profile and comparative clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Independent validation of a predictive risk model for contrast-enhancing brain lesions supports enhanced periventricular radiosensitivity and variable proton RBE
articles.summary: This study validates a risk model confirming enhanced periventricular radiosensitivity and supports the implementation of LET-dependent proton RBE in treatment planning. The authors emphasize the importance of actively sparing periventricular structures to mitigate brain injury risks in proton therapy.

articles.title: A decentralized federated learning approach for predicting chemoradiotherapy response from multicenter whole-slide images
articles.summary: Researchers developed a federated learning model that predicts NSCLC outcomes from whole-slide images while maintaining data privacy across multiple institutions. This method achieved performance comparable to centralized models, offering a scalable framework for collaborative research in radiation oncology.

articles.title: Pancreatic SBRT in Italian Clinical Practice: A Multicenter Analysis of 473 Patients Treated in 17 Centers
articles.summary: This multicenter study evaluated the safety and efficacy of stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) for pancreatic cancer. Findings suggest that ablative dose delivery and MR-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT) improve local control and organ-at-risk protection in non-metastatic patients.

articles.title: Vascular and Circulating Blood Exposure to Proton or Photon Irradiation: Differentials in Lymphocyte Subset Metrics in Cancer Patients
articles.summary: This study demonstrates that patient-specific vascular delineation and dosimetry can track irradiation modality and correlate with lymphocyte depletion. The authors suggest that immune-sparing plan optimization using vascular constraints is a feasible area for future clinical development.

articles.title: In Silico Dosimetric Comparison of Intensity-Modulated Photon Versus Proton Therapy for Pelvic and Para-Aortic Nodal Recurrence of Prostate Cancer Following Prior Irradiation
articles.summary: This dosimetric study evaluates the differences between VMAT and IMPT for treating nodal recurrences in a re-irradiation setting. The research provides valuable planning comparisons for optimizing dose distribution in complex, previously irradiated cases.

articles.title: Optimization and Performance Assessment of a Low-Dose Alanine Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Dosimetry Procedure for Potential Application in Electron Beam FLASH Radiotherapy
articles.summary: Researchers optimized alanine EPR dosimetry to improve accuracy for dose measurements below 10 Gy. This technical development is significant for the clinical quality assurance and validation requirements of emerging high-dose-rate FLASH radiotherapy treatments.

articles.title: Comparative assessment of respiratory-induced tumor motion using fluoroscopy and four-dimensional CT of solitary pulmonary lesions
articles.summary: This study compared respiratory motion measurements derived from fluoroscopy and 4DCT in patients undergoing proton therapy planning. Findings revealed larger absolute differences in motion measurements for lower-lobe tumors, suggesting that 4DCT-based estimations should be interpreted with caution in such cases.

articles.title: Prognostic Evidence for Artificial Intelligence-Derived PET Tumour-Burden Biomarkers in Cancer: A Systematic Review
articles.summary: This systematic review evaluates the current evidence for AI-automated tumour-burden measurements on PET scans, such as metabolic tumour volume (MTV). It explores the prognostic value of these AI-derived biomarkers in comparison to traditional expert manual measurements in clinical oncology.

articles.title: Proton-Induced Bystander Signaling Drives Cell-Type-Specific Proteomic Remodeling in Chondrocytes and Endothelial Cells
articles.summary: This experimental study examines how proton-induced bystander signals influence proteomic changes in non-irradiated cells. The findings identify distinct pathway activations depending on the recipient cell type, providing a basis for further exploration of radiation-induced biological effects.

articles.title: CY 2027 Medicare Final Rules and Impact on Proton Therapy
articles.summary: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) released final rules for the CY 2027 Physician Fee Schedule and Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System. The ruling includes a significant increase in hospital outpatient reimbursement rates for proton therapy due to budget-neutral redistribution, though standalone centers express concern regarding potential future financial impacts.

articles.title: BayCare Proton Center Treats First Patient on Mevion S250 FIT™ with Leo Cancer Care's Marie® Solution
articles.summary: The BayCare Proton Center has successfully initiated patient treatments using the Mevion S250 FIT proton therapy system integrated with Leo Cancer Care's Marie solution. This installation marks a new technological implementation in a clinical setting for advanced proton delivery.

articles.title: 50 million Americans live in counties without a radiation oncology clinic, study finds
articles.summary: A recent study highlights that 50 million Americans reside in counties lacking a radiation oncology clinic, underscoring significant geographic disparities in access to cancer care. The findings emphasize the ongoing challenges in providing equitable radiation treatment coverage across the United States.

articles.title: ASTRO updates guideline on shorter-course radiation therapy for localized prostate cancer
articles.summary: The American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO) has updated its clinical guidelines regarding the use of shorter-course radiation therapy for patients with localized prostate cancer. The update reflects evolving clinical evidence on hypofractionated treatment regimens.

articles.title: IBA treats first patient in clinical trial of FLASH proton therapy for head and neck cancer
articles.summary: IBA has announced the treatment of the first patient in the C-FLASH-01 clinical trial, evaluating the safety and efficacy of ConformalFLASH proton therapy. This trial marks a significant milestone in testing ultra-high dose rate radiation delivery for head and neck cancer patients.

articles.title: Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute opens new wellness space
articles.summary: The Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute has inaugurated a new wellness facility dedicated to supporting patients and their caregivers. This regional development enhances the supportive care infrastructure at this key proton therapy center in the DMV area.
